pullRequests.title: fix(tools): us_port.py renames the names of a port in one pass
pullRequests.author: llesieur99
pullRequests.head: fix/us-port-simultaneous-renames
pullRequests.body:
us_port.py turned each relocated name into its NTSC-U address one name at a time. When the
NTSC-U address of one name is the PAL address of another name the block also uses, the second
rename caught the first one's result as well, and the two names became one: a port that reads two
globals would read one of them twice. The same could happen to the function's own name and to the
callee twins renamed after it.
The renames are now made in one pass (rename_all), so a new name is never renamed…

pullRequests.head: feat/sister-twins
pullRequests.body:
Purpose
tools/sister_twins.py finds rac3 functions that are still in assembly and whose code is a function another OpenRAC decompilation has already matched in C. The sister's C can then be ported instead of written again. A twin is exact when every relocation-masked word is equal, and near (20 words and more) when at least 95 % of them are.
The tool turns the one-off scan scripts of 2026-11-15 into a reusable tool. That scan found 203 twins (179 exact), and porting their C gave dozens of…

commits.author: llesieur99
commits.body:
us_port.py turned each relocated name into its NTSC-U address one name at a time. When the
NTSC-U address of one name is the PAL address of another name the block also uses, the second
rename caught the first one's result as well, and the two names became one: a port that reads two
globals would read one of them twice. The same could happen to the function's own name and to the
callee twins renamed after it.

The renames are now made in one pass (rename_all), so a new name is never renamed…
